runs.text: A NAO-centred ROS 2 architecture for grounded dialogue, structured planning, deterministic execution, and evidence-based reporting.
Juan David Bendek Williamson    •    Supervised by Raquel Ros    •    2025–2026
MSc Modelling for Science and Engineering

Timing: 1:00. Open with the system problem, not the implementation history. Thank Raquel Ros, IIIA-CSIC, SocialMinds, and the JAE-ICU programme in one sentence, then state that the thesis concerns the complete interaction architecture and its qualification boundaries.
A plausible plan is not yet a safe robot action.
• Users refer to people, objects, and prior turns.
• One request can mix dialogue, knowledge, and action.
• A fluent plan can still omit targets or invent unsupported behaviour.
• Capabilities and arguments must be checked before dispatch.
• Identity, order, and lineage must survive execution.
• Completion must follow typed results and verified effects.
Example: “Bring all the objects you can see to ALEX.”

Timing: 1:30. Use the ALEX example. Explain that correct execution requires route choice, role preservation, complete target selection, valid plan coverage, execution evidence, and truthful final reporting.
The study asks how flexibility can be integrated without surrendering execution control.

How can a modular robot architecture integrate dialogue, symbolic grounding, planning, deterministic execution, and feedback while preserving clear responsibility boundaries and evidence-based communication?
dialogue, grounding, planning, orchestration, and skills through explicit ROS 2 interfaces
candidate plans through reviewed capabilities and deterministic admission before dispatch
full turns, controlled failures, symbolic postconditions, and truthful reporting
Timing: 1:30. State the central question once. The three objective verbs compress the seven thesis objectives. Map the five research questions to plans, grounding, admission, recovery, and ownership.
The architecture contains model variation instead of assuming it away.
Generated outputs enter typed request and plan contracts.
Unsupported skills, roles, arguments, and incomplete coverage are rejected.
The orchestrator controls ordered dispatch and plan lineage.
Typed results and postconditions constrain user-facing claims.
Deterministic interfaces do not make generation deterministic. They make variation attributable and restrict its execution authority.
Timing: 1:25. This is the thesis in one slide. Emphasise that safe rejection is useful but still counts as a task-level failure.
Each uncertainty has an owner, and evidence returns through the same lineage.
Goal ID  •  plan ID  •  plan version  •  stable step IDs
KnowledgeCore and scene grounding provide bounded entities, roles, locations, and relations.
Robot-facing or simulated adapters return the same typed result boundary.

Timing: 2:00. Walk left to right. Dialogue owns speech. The chatbot routes and grounds. The planner proposes. The orchestrator validates and dispatches. Skills return evidence. The same lineage reaches one final dialogue act.
Explicit interfaces separate proposal quality from execution safety.
Safe rejection prevents invalid dispatch, but it does not convert an incomplete plan into success.
Timing: 1:35. Mention the reviewed skill registry and the key contracts: planner request, skill description, plan envelope, execution feedback, result, and dialogue act. Do not enumerate every field.
Available context supports a decision, but fresh evidence proves an action.
Speech, posture and head motion were integrated. Look-at used a real adapter, while the primary profile remained fake-by-default.
Navigation, find, pick, place, bring, walk and wave exposed deterministic success and failure outcomes through the same result contract.
The detector and physical manipulation remain separate evidence seams.

Timing: 1:30. Explain the distinction between grounded availability and authoritative selection. Be exact about the physical boundary: the thesis validates software and symbolic effects more deeply than navigation, grasping, or detector accuracy.
A case passed only when semantics, execution, effects, and reporting agreed.
Correct dialogue, knowledge, or execution path
Complete targets, roles, skills, order, and lineage
Success, failure, clarification, or bounded replan
Postcondition and final report agree with evidence
One unit of analysis = one user request under a fixed software, model, world-state, and skill configuration.
Scenario-based software and integration validation, not unrestricted robot-task success or human-subject evaluation.

Timing: 1:40. Explain that event presence alone was insufficient. The harness compared requested, selected, planned, executed, and reported target sets; role integrity; ordered constraints; KB postconditions; report coverage; and exactly-once speech.
One primary qualification anchors the thesis; other model probes remain separate.
Derived from 33 structured runtime traces across the final evidence index.
Qwen3-VL: 64 passes and 8 failures under the frozen qualification.
Three Ollama models, retained outside the primary denominator.
The 22-case end-to-end questionnaire produced 20 passes and 2 failures.
Timing: 1:20. Keep denominators explicit. The 191 supplementary observations do not enlarge or replace the 72-record primary qualification.
Incomplete plans were rejected before dispatch. Safe containment did not erase task-level failure.
Timing: 1:50. Read the exact counts, not only the percentages. Use the 8.4 score later, after the evidence components. State that not all 72 records were physical robot turns.
The remaining failures occur at identifiable semantic and closure boundaries.
KB update entered the execution planner
One member omitted from an “all objects” set
Kitchen treated as the delivery recipient
Required action absent from a long composite
Recovery occurred without reliable terminal speech
The architecture converted silent execution risks into inspectable route, selection, plan, clarification, or closure failures.

Timing: 1:30. Distinguish containment from repair. The architecture caught the two incomplete capability-extreme plans, but target selection, role assignment, clarification, and closure still depended partly on model output.
Stable interfaces did not produce invariant semantic behaviour.
Qwen3-VL completed the frozen campaign. A compatible replacement must pass the same campaign before inheriting qualification.
Model-agnostic describes the interface boundary. Model-invariant would require equivalent behaviour, which the evidence did not show.
Timing: 1:30. Qwen3.5 and Ollama evidence was narrower and mostly screening-level. The final Gemma fallback passed preflight and one dialogue smoke turn only.
A failed pick produced a revised plan without losing the completed work.
The model did not directly retry the robot. It proposed plan version 2 after receiving structured failure evidence.
It demonstrates middle-stage recovery, retained lineage, and a truthful closure. Beginning-stage navigation recovery was also retained; terminal recovery remained less reliable.

Timing: 1:35. This is retained evidence, not a staged live run. The corresponding beginning-stage navigation trace preserved a four-target objective and closed. Later-stage delivery and missing-recipient cases were less complete.
Three short turns expose dialogue, knowledge, and execution routing.
answer from the declared symbolic state
accepted plan, one skill result, one closure
The demonstration illustrates the architecture. The frozen traces remain the scored evidence.

Timing: 1:30 maximum. Show rqt input and the trace viewer side by side. Allow about 25 seconds per turn. If a response stalls, stop immediately, state that the live run is illustrative rather than scored, and continue to the retained evidence. Do not change models, relaunch nodes, or troubleshoot during the defence. If the robot is present, the third turn may use real head motion and TTS. Without the robot, use the deterministic adapter and show the typed result.
The strongest evidence concerns software contracts and symbolic state.
• unrestricted autonomy or universal model ranking
Another robot needs an equivalent reviewed skill registry and typed adapters. Another model must repeat the frozen qualification.
Controlled simulation reduced hardware variance and compute waste, but it cannot replace physical safety and performance measurement.

Timing: 1:35. Cover ethics and sustainability briefly: execution authority remains bounded; no human-subject or safety claim is made; controlled adapters reduce unnecessary robot trials and enable reproducibility. Transfer remains an architectural proposition until measured on another platform.
The thesis result is preserved as one reproducible configuration.
Reviewed branch and nested fork commits.
Secondary summary of the explicit case evidence.
The score summarises qualification; the denominators and failure reasons carry the claim.
Timing: 1:05. The final tag is an alias of the validated image, not a rebuild after evaluation. Keep the operational index secondary to case counts.
Move from validated software contracts toward measured embodiment.
Quantify head and gaze behaviour, guarded wave, bounded local motion, semantic navigation, and pointing kinematics.
Evaluate detector identity settling and scene-grounding quality before promoting detector-derived facts into stronger claims.
Measure ASR, TTS, latency, interruption handling, and autonomous idle/request arbitration with users and physical trials.
Every promoted skill should begin with one physical success, one failure or cancellation, and the same typed evidence boundary.

Timing: 1:20. Keep LocateAnything and broader detector work as future work. The immediate physical path is real head/gaze and wave, followed by navigation and manipulation only when spatial and safety evidence is available.
The thesis contributes an architecture, a containment boundary, and a qualification method.
A modular ownership model connecting dialogue, grounding, planning, execution, and reporting.
Typed contracts and deterministic admission restrict model-generated execution authority.
A repeatable evidence method separates model, stack, observability, and physical claims.
Together, these boundaries make language-model variation observable without hiding task-level failure.
Timing: 1:05. These are the three contributions to leave in the committee's notes. Avoid claiming a first or universal architecture.

Language-model dialogue and planning can participate in an integrated robot architecture when their outputs are grounded, validated against reviewed skills, dispatched deterministically, and checked against typed feedback and symbolic postconditions.
The boundaries do not eliminate non-determinism. They make it observable and restrict its execution authority.
Thank you. I welcome your questions.
Timing: 1:00. Pause after the second statement. Thank the committee. Do not introduce new future work during the conclusion.
Five frozen cases repeated three times

Direct support for fail-once navigation and pick
Missing-object, recipient, and closure recovery remained partial
Supported at interface and auditability level
Other robots and equivalent model behaviour remain unqualified
Use this slide when a committee member asks for a direct answer to one or more research questions.
Use when asked exactly what was held constant or which physical components were exercised.
Proceed live only if preflight is green
• one model endpoint advertised and probed
• rqt input and trace viewer visible
• robot adapter selected before the defence
• do not relaunch or switch models on stage
• state that the live run is illustrative and the retained campaign is scored
Maximum live window: 90 seconds. No troubleshooting inside the timed defence.
This appendix is for presenter recovery. If the live run fails, return to slide 13 or continue to slide 15 without apology or debugging.
They place repeatable outcomes at the robot-facing result boundary, isolating planning and recovery from hardware variance.
Admission, schema checks, dispatch order, lineage, feedback correlation, and effect verification. Route and plan generation remain model-dependent.
The interfaces accept multiple backends. The results explicitly show that semantic behaviour is not invariant.
The thesis validates integration and containment, not a causal comparison of planning algorithms.
Quantified physical skills, detector-quality evaluation, and user-facing interaction trials under the same evidence contracts.
Keep the first answer under 30 seconds. Expand only when the committee asks for additional detail.
Integrate dialogue, routing, grounding, planning, deterministic orchestration, and skills through ROS 2 interfaces.
Define explicit runtime contracts for requests, context, plans, results, feedback, dialogue acts, and raw evidence.
Expose capabilities through a reviewed skill registry rather than model-generated robot APIs.
Support dialogue, knowledge, atomic, and composite turns without transferring speech or execution ownership.
Validate plans before dispatch and return typed evidence for failure, clarification, replanning, and reporting.
Exercise full turns, controlled outcomes, focused subsystem checks, and symbolic postconditions.
Use if the committee asks for the complete objective list beyond the three objective verbs shown in the main presentation.
